_README: HUMAN GROUND TRUTH for speaker attribution. The owner watched and listened to the
passage and wrote the turns out by hand. This is the only turn-level gold data in
the project, and it is the yardstick any diarization or 'sensing' approach must be
measured against. Nothing in here is machine-derived.
`turns` is the owner's text, verbatim and in order, with the owner's speaker labels.
`anchor` is NOT owner-provided: it records which textual cue identifies that speaker,
added during analysis so the cues can be tested as features. Treat `speaker` as fact
WHY THIS EXISTS. qa_check and check_figures are both 0/68 and neither reads whether a
turn holds two voices. 341 published turns of 400+ words across 63 episodes sit under
one label. The standing rule is never to infer a speaker from text, because register,
sentence-continuation, word-overlap and caption '>>' markers have each been measurably
wrong on this corpus. Gold data changes the task from blind inference to measurable
validation: a cue is allowed only if it scores well HERE first.

2026-08-28-ep61.region: roughly 01:30 to 03:00, the post-jacket schedule exchange into the first Beria item
2026-08-28-ep61.owner_note: OK, this is the most accurate based on what I hear and watch.

turns.text: Okay baik YB. Cuti panjang, YB buat apa?

turns.text: Ahad di Puchong, betul-betul Puchong lah, HQ kita punya.

turns.speaker: Rafizi
